payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-08-12
payload.summary:
**Codex lands on Linux** and OpenAI hints at another Codex surprise; **Gemini flexes platform reach** with 100M+ active iOS users and deeper Android app actions; Anthropic voices push **adversarial code review** and text watermarking as AI code shifts from syntax bugs to system-level misses; the big undercurrent: AI keeps moving off the screen, from **Samsara’s physical-world deployment** to enterprise-heavy FDE work and vertical open-weight plays.

**Codex 上 Linux 了**，OpenAI 还在给明天埋包袱；**Gemini 开始晒盘子**，iOS 过亿活跃用户，Android 继续往跨应用操作上推；Anthropic 那边一手讲 **对抗式审查代码**，一手把文本水印和检测 API 往前送；更有意思的是，AI 话题明显不只停在聊天框里了，从 **Samsara** 把模型塞进车队和工地，到企业里那种又脏又重的 FDE 落地活，都开始变得具体。

sections.headline: **Samsara** says the biggest AI rollout may be in the physical world · **Samsara** 说，最大的 AI 部署可能根本不在屏幕里
sections.body:
On **The MAD Podcast**, **Matt Turck** talks with **Samsara** CEO **Sanjit Biswas** about what he frames as one of the largest real-world AI deployments: millions of vehicles, roughly **25 trillion data points a year**, and systems that touch **99% of US roads** daily. The core argument is straightforward: the physical world has always been harder for AI because the data is messy, the hardware is real, and mistakes can hurt people. That is also why the upside is so large.

Biswas describes **physical AI** less as humanoid theater and more as instrumentation plus action: GPS, cameras, weather, vehicle data, and workflow software fused into systems that can flag risk, guide workers, and increasingly trigger work. He says **Samsara** helped prevent about **380,000 road accidents** last year and argues the next wave of AI value will come from infrastructure, logistics, utilities, and construction rather than pure software alone.

在这期 **The MAD Podcast** 里，**Matt Turck** 找来 **Samsara** CEO **Sanjit Biswas**，聊的不是聊天机器人，而是很硬的现实世界部署：几百万辆车、每年大约 **25 万亿**条数据、每天覆盖 **99% 的美国道路**。核心意思不复杂：物理世界一直更难做，因为数据乱、硬件真要装、出错还可能伤人。也正因为这样，价值才大。

Biswas 讲的 **physical AI**，也不是那种只拿人形机器人吸眼球的版本，而是把 GPS、摄像头、天气、车辆和作业流程数据拧在一起，先看清现场，再给出动作，最后慢慢走向自动执行。他提到 **Samsara** 去年大概帮助避免了 **38 万起道路事故**，判断下一波真正见效的 AI，会更多落在基础设施、物流、公用事业和工地这些地方，而不只是软件界面里。

sections.headline: LLM bugs have shifted from syntax slips to system design misses, says Boris Cherny · Boris Cherny 说，LLM 的 bug 已从语法小错转向系统设计层面
sections.body:
LLMs still produce bugs, but those bugs are different than what they used to be. It’s less off-by-ones and more about system design, ui usability, missing broader context. Some kinds of coding has been solved, but not all.

While models continue to improve, adversarial code review has been an incredibly powerful tool to catch many of these kinds of bugs.

It can be as simple as a one line prompt - “use a dynamic workflow to adversarial test every edge case in an iOS simulator”, or use Claude’s built in /code-review (or /code-review low, /code-review medium, etc.)

LLM 还是会产出 bug，但这些 bug 和以前不一样了。现在少了很多 off-by-one 这种错误，更多变成系统设计、UI 可用性、缺少更大上下文这类问题。有些类型的编程已经被解决了，但不是全部。

模型还在继续变强，但对抗式代码审查一直是个非常有效的工具，能抓住很多这类 bug。

它甚至可以简单到只用一行提示词，比如：“use a dynamic workflow to adversarial test every edge case in an iOS simulator”，或者直接用 Claude 内置的 /code-review（也可以是 /code-review low、/code-review medium 等）。

sections.headline: A 2023 prompt-log surprise now looks obvious: people wanted app-building agents · 2023 年看着很野的需求，到现在已经快成现实：用户就是想让模型直接做应用
sections.body:
story time..

in 2023 (my previous role) I remember the first time some customers volunteered their prompt logs to us. 

We were surprised by the number of “build me an app for X” prompts.

felt wildly ambitious at the time. models were barely graduating from code completion to generating a useful block of code.

But it was a great signal of what people actually wanted, and shaped a lot of our vision: systems that could design, build and deploy an app end to end from a simple ask.

Pretty wild that 3 yrs later we’re basically there.

讲个小故事……

2023 年的时候（我上一份工作），我还记得第一次有客户主动把他们的 prompt logs 给我们看。

我们当时很惊讶，里面有那么多“build me an app for X”这样的提示。

放在当时看，这野心大得离谱。那会儿模型才刚从代码补全，勉强走到能生成一段有用代码的阶段。

但这其实是个很强的信号，说明用户真正想要什么；它也塑造了我们很多愿景：做出那种从一句简单需求出发，就能设计、构建、部署完整应用的系统。

挺夸张的，3 年后我们基本已经走到这儿了。

sections.headline: Open-weight models can win by going painfully deep into boring business domains · 开源权重模型还有大钱可赚，前提是死磕那些无聊但真实的行业场景
sections.body:
There’s going to be a ton of money in making open-weight models exceptional at boring, specific business domains.

Pick a size x domain combination and go deep. Eg mid-market legal, smb retail, enterprise logistics. 

The hyperscalers have the primitives but will struggle with domain depth, scrappiness and sheer will to make a model exceptional for one particular kind of business.

And that is your opportunity.

把 open-weight models 做到某个具体、无聊、但真有业务价值的领域里特别能打，这里面会有很多钱。

选一个 size x domain 的组合，然后狠狠干深。比如中型法律业务、SMB 零售、企业物流。

大云厂商有底层能力，但在领域深度、灵活劲儿，还有那种非把一个模型为某类业务做到极致的狠劲上，往往会吃亏。

这就是你的机会。

sections.headline: Aaron Levie says FDE work is real, messy, and not going away in AI · Aaron Levie 说，FDE 这活在 AI 里是真脏真重，而且短期不会消失
sections.body:
Good post on how to think about FDEs. The key is that FDEs are real and not going away for AI any time soon.

The reason this is happening now at a scale that has never been seen before is because AI is fundamentally about adding a non-deterministic, rapidly changing system to workflows that largely have never been automated before. This looks very little like implementing traditional software.

“If you're building an AI agent for accounting in 2026, there is no established workflow, because literally nobody has ever used one of these. Nobody knows what the user journey looks like — not you, and importantly, not your customer either. They can't tell you what they want, because the thing they'd want doesn't have a shape yet.”

Software has largely always been deterministic and once implemented effectively worked the same for customers. This meant the upfront implementation work was *relatively* uniform across similar customers, and the system wasn’t regularly being upgraded in fundamental ways. 

AI agents are entirely different on nearly every dimension. The customer’s business process has to change to work with agents, there is heavy -necessary- customization to get agents to work in the customers end-state process, evals need to be run constantly, the AI models are constantly changing and updates need to keep getting incorporated, the underlying harness and broader system are often changing due to customer feedback, and much more. 

This is real work for the customer, systems integrators, and the applied AI vendors. Even as AI capabilities improve dramatically, this work remains (or even gets more complicated) given enterprises will just throw increasingly more complex processes at agents. Great time to be an FDE.

这篇文章对怎么理解 FDE 写得不错。关键点在于：FDE 在 AI 里是真需求，而且短时间内不会消失。

之所以现在会以过去没见过的规模爆发，是因为 AI 本质上是在把一个非确定、变化飞快的系统，塞进那些以前大多根本没自动化过的工作流里。这和部署传统软件，长得真不太像。

“如果你在 2026 年给会计场景做 AI agent，其实根本没有现成工作流，因为字面意义上没人真正用过这类东西。没人知道用户旅程该长什么样，不是你不知道，关键是客户自己也不知道。他们说不清自己想要什么，因为那个东西还没有成形。”

过去的软件大多是确定性的，一旦部署好，对不同客户的工作方式也相对一致。所以前期实施工作在相似客户之间，通常也相对统一，而且系统本身不会频繁发生根本性变化。

AI agents 在几乎每个维度上都不一样。客户的业务流程得为了 agent 改；为了让 agent 适配客户最终要的流程，重度定制往往不可避免；eval 要一直跑；模型在不停变，更新得不断接；底层 harness 和更大的系统也会因为客户反馈持续变化，等等。

这就是实打实的工作，落在客户、系统集成商和应用型 AI 厂商头上。就算 AI 能力继续猛涨，这些活也不会自然消失，甚至可能更复杂，因为企业只会把更难的流程继续扔给 agents。现在做 FDE，时机不差。
